questionProposals.contentQualification: These are supplied broad category descriptions, not inferred incident facts. National goals alone do not verify sponsorship; resources and zero-days are not universal state/APT requirements. Low expertise is explicit; public tools alone do not prove it. Ideology is a motive and entrusted access a relationship, not universal technique or malicious intent. Organised financial crime is a contextual category, not proof that all money-seeking attacks are nonstate. The drill covers five types but no Shadow IT, real attribution, threat-vector analysis, advanced capability verification or all2.1 motivations. No part or option is an independent mastery assessment.

questionProposals.contentQualification: The title/task says motivations, but delivered examples mix sponsorship, capability, access/intent and motive. Government sponsorship, organisation for profit, ideological protest, deliberate insider misuse and inexperience are explicit premises; the learner mostly recognises labels from those premises. Grievance alone does not establish insider status or malicious intent, and a public tool/name, financial goal, duration or disruptive technique alone establishes no sponsor, capability or actor identity. APT is not a nation-state synonym. No independent incident investigation, attack-surface decision or general motivation-to-actor attribution is demonstrated; five parts are not five eligible mastery observations.

partSemanticInspections.teachingUnderstanding: An expressly organised criminal profit example supplies the category, rather than inferring it from a malware technique.
Government sponsorship is stated, rather than inferred from duration, custom tools or national leverage.
An expressly ideological protest example supplies motive; service disruption does not uniquely identify an actor.
Deliberate misuse and authorised employee access are both stated; grievance alone would not establish malicious-insider attribution.
Explicit inexperience supports low-capability vocabulary; ready-made tools and recognition motive alone would not prove low skill.
